title: identity.session.revoked payload
description: The `data` payload of the `identity.session.revoked` event: every credential a user holds was ended by one of identity's own flows. Three fields. The second, `email`, travels because both notices this event can trigger are mailed — "your password was changed" (reason `password reset`) and "your email address was changed" (reason `email address changed`) — and the fleet's consumer is cross-service: courier has no identity client, no identity credentials and no identity tables, so the address is not a fact it can read from the user row (REPORT-courier-consumer-invite-01.md §2.6). The publisher refuses to build the payload without it, for the same fail-closed reason it refuses a reason it does not implement. The third is a CLOSED SET OF TWO that the publisher validates before it appends, which is what makes it safe for a consumer to switch on. A single logout is not this event: `DELETE /v1/session` ends ONE session and emits nothing, so a subscriber may read this type as "this account's credentials are all gone, drop whatever you cached against them" without a field telling it so. There is no count and no list of session ids, because the publisher has already ended them all by the time the row commits and a frozen list on the bus would be a second thing to keep in sync. The envelope is validated by schemas/event-envelope.schema.json; this schema validates what is inside `data`. The file path is the event type with dots as directory separators. See docs/event-naming.md.

user_id.description: The user whose credentials are gone. Always equal to the envelope's `subject`, so a consumer can key on either. A bare uuid rather than a `usr_`-prefixed id: that is what identity's `id.UUID.String()` produces, and it is the same value courier and billing already key users on (D7).

email.description: The address the user holds when the event is built, normalized (lower-cased, trimmed) exactly as every other address on the bus is. Both notices this event can trigger are mailed to it, and the consumer that mails them is cross-service: courier has no identity client, no identity credentials and no identity tables, so the address is not a fact it can read from the user row (REPORT-courier-consumer-invite-01.md §2.6). For the email-change reason this is the NEW address — the move and the event are one transaction, so the row holds the new one when the builder reads it; which address that is, and why, is recorded in REPORT-identity-event-payloads-01.md.

reason.description: Which flow ended them. A closed set of two, and the values are the publisher's own constants — it refuses a reason this build does not implement rather than publishing a string no consumer can switch on. A consumer acting on the event sometimes needs to know whether to expect a sign-in, and this is the field that says. The entity is `session` and the value is plural on purpose: no single session was revoked, every credential the user held was.
